summary: A TypeScript library (in memory; the library itself has zero runtime dependencies, Express is the one dependency and it is confined to the optional stage 7 HTTP layer) for the core of a password manager: a master password unlocks storage for a user's OTHER credentials, encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM, built in seven stages. Stage 1: the master password itself is never stored, not even hashed separately -- only a random salt and a canary ciphertext (a fixed plaintext encrypted once at vault creation with the key derived via scrypt from the real master password); unlocking derives a candidate key and tries to decrypt the canary, and AES-GCM's own authentication tag is the entire pass/fail signal. Lockout after MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS (5) wrong attempts via an injectable Clock, changeMasterPassword's own check going through the identical lockout gate as unlock() so it cannot be used as an unrated side door for guessing; changeMasterPassword re-encrypts every entry atomically; a generatePassword utility using crypto.randomInt, never Math.random. Stage 2: saving an entry becomes a real async call to a VaultStore (the one place two devices can genuinely race each other); unlock() returns a sessionId so several devices can each hold their own session on the SAME vault; every mutating operation brackets its one await with a SYNCHRONOUS claim before it and an apply or release after (mirrored from this repo's 17-parking-lot project's reserve/confirm), so a master-password rotation and any in-flight add/update/delete can never overlap -- fixing a real lost-update bug where a concurrently-added entry, still encrypted under the old key, would be silently discarded by the rotation's wholesale replace of the entries map; a per-entry version number gives two concurrent edits of the SAME entry ENTRY_CONFLICT for the loser instead of silent data loss; a generation counter invalidates every OTHER session immediately when the password changes, checked lazily, never by walking every session. Stage 3: breach checking via the real k-anonymity protocol Have I Been Pwned's password API uses -- only the first 5 hex characters of a password's SHA-1 hash ever leave isPasswordBreached; a small self-contained CircuitBreaker (closed/open/half-open) plus a per-call timeout protect the save path, and a breach check can NEVER block a save (the opposite instinct from this project's usual "an error means nothing happened" rule, deliberately): a provider error, a timeout, or an open circuit all degrade to breached: null. Stage 4: sharing a single entry between two INDEPENDENT vaults via hybrid/envelope encryption (RSA-OAEP wraps a fresh one-time AES key; the entry content itself is AES-256-GCM like everywhere else, the same pattern TLS and PGP use); each vault lazily generates its own RSA-2048 keypair only on first use (about 200ms, so never paid on every createVault); the private key is stored only encrypted under the vault's own key, and changeMasterPassword re-wraps it on every rotation -- a real gap caught and fixed before it could silently and permanently brick sharing the moment a vault's owner changed their password; redeemShare unwraps the envelope and then calls the recipient's own addEntry, so a shared credential automatically gets the same claim/commit exclusion and the same breach check as any other entry, with no duplicated logic. Stage 5: share revocation and single-use redemption -- a manager-wide shares registry (the same role sessions already plays, never vault content); redeemShare claims the grant synchronously, before any await, the identical claim-before-await shape as stage 2's claimEntryOp now protecting a different resource, so two concurrent redemptions of the same token can never both succeed; a precondition failure (NO_SHARING_KEY) is checked and thrown BEFORE that claim since it is not a real attempt, while a genuine failure after claiming releases it so a real retry still gets its one legitimate shot; revokeShare reports an unknown shareId and someone-else's shareId identically (UNKNOWN_SHARE) -- the same don't-leak-existence instinct as not telling a failed login which part was wrong. Stage 6: sessions auto-lock after sessionIdleTimeoutMs of inactivity (default 15 minutes) via LAZY expiry at requireSession -- the single choke point every session-based call already goes through -- never a background timer, consistent with the lockout cooldown and SESSION_INVALIDATED already being lazy checks; isSessionActive is a pure read that never itself resets the idle clock, since a status check that could keep a session alive just by being polled would defeat the whole point; each session carries its own independent lastActivityAt, so one idle device never affects another device's active session on the same vault. Stage 7: an Express HTTP API (4.22.3, matching this repo's 21-notification project's pinned version) in front of the whole library, authenticating services with one constant-time bearer API key, the same scope as 21-notification's API; every PasswordManagerErrorCode maps to a specific HTTP status (none to 500, since every one of the library's own error codes is an expected, documented outcome); asyncRoute() wraps every route calling an async PasswordManager method because Express 4, unlike Express 5, does not route a rejected promise to its error handler automatically. 140 tests total (stage 1: 48; stage 2 added 15; stage 3 added 27; stage 4 added 16; stage 5 added 7; stage 6 added 9; stage 7 added 18), including a randomized invariant test (4 seeds x 150 sequential operations against a shadow model) and a dedicated concurrency test file reproducing and fixing each real race directly, plus a standalone illustration of the un-guarded version of the bug for contrast. Mutation checks, each break applied alone with the file restored byte for byte: 128 total across all seven stages, all caught (one more attempted break, on the stage 5 revocation wiring, was discovered to be malformed -- it moved a check into a spot an earlier, unrelated check already made provably unreachable -- and was discarded rather than counted, the same principle as a stage 1 check that found genuinely unreachable dead code in the password generator and had that code removed rather than tested). Not built: a real persisted storage backend (VaultStore is in-memory only), a real breach-check network call (FakeBreachProvider is a fixed in-memory dataset), a directory service for exchanging sharing public keys, 2FA, CORS or a browser-facing session layer on the HTTP API, rate limiting independent of the vault's own lockout, a background sweep that proactively evicts idle sessions, revoking or expiring an ALREADY-redeemed share, password-strength scoring beyond the generator's own charset rules.

pitch.intro_30s: Maine ek password manager ka core banaya hai, TypeScript mein, in memory, saat stages mein. Master password kabhi store nahi hota, sirf ek canary ciphertext decrypt karke verify hota hai. Do devices same vault unlock kar sakte hain, aur har mutation ek synchronous claim ke peeche apna await rakhta hai taaki race na ho. Breach check k-anonymity se hota hai, sharing hybrid encryption se do alag vaults ke beech, revocation aur single-use shares, idle session auto-lock, aur upar ek HTTP API. 140 tests, 128 mutation checks, sab caught.
pitch.explain_2min:
'Design a password manager' interview mein kai alag angles se poocha jaata hai: encryption-at-rest (master password kaise verify karoge bina store kiye), concurrency (do devices same vault, same entry edit karen to kya hoga), aur ek credential doosre user ko kaise securely bhejoge. Maine saat stages mein yahi follow-ups chhote, tested rules banaye.

Stage 1: master password ek canary ciphertext ke through verify hota hai -- fixed plaintext jo vault banate waqt uske derived key se encrypt hota hai; unlock par candidate key se decrypt try karo, AES-GCM ka auth tag hi pass/fail hai. 5 wrong attempts ke baad lockout, aur changeMasterPassword bhi usi lockout gate se guzarta hai taaki guessing ka side door na bane.

Stage 2: saving ek real async VaultStore call ban jaati hai -- yahi jagah hai jahan do devices genuinely race kar sakte hain. Har mutation apne ek await ko ek SYNCHRONOUS claim mein wrap karta hai (17-parking-lot ke reserve/confirm jaisa) -- isse rotation aur koi in-flight add/update kabhi overlap nahi karte. Yeh exact bug fix karta hai: rotation ka wholesale replace, bagair claim ke, ek concurrent add ko silently discard kar deta.

Stage 3: breach check real k-anonymity protocol se, sirf password ke SHA-1 hash ka 5-char prefix bahar jaata hai. Circuit breaker aur timeout ensure karte hain ki ek down breach service kabhi save ko block na kare.

Stage 4 aur 5: sharing hybrid encryption se (RSA-OAEP ek one-time AES key wrap karta hai), aur har share single-use hai, claim-before-await se protected -- bilkul stage 2 jaisa pattern, lekin ek alag resource ke liye.

Stage 6: idle sessions lazily expire hote hain, background timer nahi.

Stage 7: ek HTTP API, Express 4 ke saath, jahan har library error code ek specific status par map hota hai.

140 tests, 128 mutation checks, sab caught.
pitch.deep_5min:
Ek credential ki journey, phone se Bob tak, phir password rotate hone tak.

Vault banna aur unlock. Alice createVault('alice', masterPassword) karti hai -- salt banta hai, scrypt se key derive hoti hai, aur ek fixed canary plaintext isi key se encrypt ho ke store hoti hai. Vault locked shuru hota hai, koi session nahi. Phone aur laptop dono unlock('alice', masterPassword) call karte hain -- har unlock candidate key derive karta hai aur canary decrypt try karta hai; AES-GCM ka auth tag galat key par khud fail ho jaata hai, isliye ek alag password hash store karne ki zaroorat nahi padti. Dono calls apna apna sessionId paate hain, dono independent, generation field vault ke current generation (0) ko capture karte hain.

Entry add karna. Phone se addEntry(sessionId, {title, username, password}) call hota hai. requireSession pehle check karta hai ki session ka generation vault ke generation se match kare (SESSION_INVALIDATED agar nahi), phir idle timeout check karta hai (SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT agar bohot der ho gayi), aur match hone par lastActivityAt reset kar deta hai -- using the session hi usse zinda rakhta hai. Phir breachChecker.check(password) start hota hai, kicked off hone ke baad hi claimEntryOp chalta hai -- yeh synchronous claim, rotating flag check karta hai aur pendingEntryOps++ karta hai, koi await se pehle. Isi wajah se agar ussi waqt koi changeMasterPassword chal rahi ho, yeh claim turant VAULT_BUSY de deta hai, bina kuch touch kiye. Claim milne ke baad hi breach-check ka result await hota hai -- CircuitBreaker ke through, agar provider down ho ya timeout ho jaaye, breached: null ban jaata hai, save kabhi block nahi hota. Entry object banta hai, encrypt hota hai session key se, aur VaultStore.persist() ko commit kiya jaata hai; sirf commit succeed hone ke baad hi record.entries.set() se in-memory map update hota hai, aur pendingEntryOps-- finally block mein.

Sharing Bob ko. Bob apne vault mein getSharingPublicKey(bobSessionId) call karta hai -- agar uske paas pehle se RSA keypair nahi hai, to generateSharingKeyPair() chalta hai (lagbhag 200ms, isliye yeh sirf first use par hota hai, har createVault par nahi), private key session key se encrypt ho ke record.wrappedPrivateKey mein store hoti hai. Alice ab shareEntry(aliceSessionId, entryId, bobPublicKey) call karti hai -- yeh pure synchronous hai: apna entry decrypt karti hai apne session key se, phir ek fresh one-time AES key banata hai, entry ka plaintext usse encrypt karta hai, aur usi one-time key ko RSA-OAEP se Bob ki public key se wrap karta hai. Ek shareId register hota hai manager-wide shares map mein, redeemedAt null, revoked false.

Bob redeem karta hai. redeemShare(bobSessionId, token) sabse pehle shareId check karta hai -- agar revoked hai to SHARE_REVOKED, agar pehle se redeemedAt set hai to SHARE_ALREADY_REDEEMED. Agar Bob ke paas abhi tak keypair nahi hai (NO_SHARING_KEY), yeh check claim se PEHLE hota hai, taaki setup na hone ki galti Bob ka ek legitimate chance na khaaye. Phir redeemedAt = now() set hota hai -- yahi claim hai, bilkul claimEntryOp jaisa, synchronous, koi await se pehle. Decrypt fail ho jaaye (jaise koi galat recipient apna private key try kare) ya Bob ka apna addEntry VAULT_BUSY de de, to catch block redeemedAt ko wapas null kar deta hai -- genuine retry ka mauka bacha rehta hai. Success par yeh seedha Bob ke apne addEntry ko call karta hai, toh Bob ki apni breach-check configuration se dobara check hota hai, uski apni claim/commit se guzarta hai -- koi duplicate logic nahi.

Alice password rotate karti hai. changeMasterPassword same lockout gate se guzarta hai jo unlock use karta hai. Agar koi entry operation ya rotation already chal rahi ho, VAULT_BUSY turant. Warna har entry purani key se decrypt, nayi key se re-encrypt hoti hai -- ek naye Map mein, record.entries ko tabhi replace karte hain jab commit succeed ho jaaye. wrappedPrivateKey bhi re-wrap hota hai, warna sharing permanently toot jaata -- yeh ek real gap tha jo dhoondha aur fix kiya gaya. generation++ hota hai, jo laptop ke purane session ko lazily invalidate kar deta hai -- next use par SESSION_INVALIDATED milega.

HTTP se bhi yeh sab same hota hai -- POST /sessions/:id/entries wagera, sirf ek asyncRoute() wrapper ke peeche kyunki Express 4 khud rejected promise ko error handler tak nahi le jaata, aur har error code ek fixed HTTP status par map hota hai.
pitch.architecture_walkthrough: src/clock.ts: Clock interface, systemClock, ManualClock -- tests time control karte hain bina sleep kiye, lockout cooldown aur idle timeout dono isi se deterministic testable hain. src/crypto.ts: encrypt/decrypt (AES-256-GCM, fresh IV har call par), deriveKey (scrypt), newSalt -- yeh har jagah reuse hota hai: canary, entries, wrappedPrivateKey, sab isi se encrypted. src/errors.ts: PasswordManagerError, ek discriminated error code type jisme 17 codes hain (INVALID_REQUEST se SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT tak). src/generator.ts: generatePassword -- crypto.randomInt (Math.random kabhi nahi), har enabled class se kam se kam ek character guaranteed, phir Fisher-Yates shuffle taaki guaranteed characters predictable position mein na rahein. src/manager.ts: sabse bada file, poora PasswordManager class -- vault lifecycle (createVault, unlock, lock, isSessionActive, getVault), entry CRUD (addEntry, getEntry, listEntries, updateEntry, deleteEntry), changeMasterPassword, exportVault, sharing (getSharingPublicKey, shareEntry, revokeShare, redeemShare), aur private helpers (requireVault, requireSession, requireEntry, claimEntryOp, commit, verifyMasterPassword, decryptBody, toSummary, toSummaryEntry). src/store.ts: VaultStore interface aur InMemoryVaultStore -- yahi ek async dependency hai poore library mein, do devices ka race yahin ban sakta hai. src/timeout.ts: withTimeout -- ek deadline ke against race karta hai, AbortSignal use karke, agar timeout ho jaaye to STORE_TIMEOUT. src/breach.ts: sha1Hex, FakeBreachProvider, isPasswordBreached -- k-anonymity, sirf 5-char hash prefix bahar jaata hai. src/circuit-breaker.ts: CircuitBreaker -- closed/open/half-open states, consecutive failures count karta hai, ek half-open trial cooldown ke baad. src/breach-checker.ts: BreachChecker -- provider, breaker, aur timeout ko jodta hai, check() kabhi throw nahi karta, hamesha boolean ya null deta hai. src/sharing.ts: generateSharingKeyPair (RSA-2048), sealForRecipient, openAsRecipient -- yeh file vaults, sessions, revocation ke baare mein kuch nahi jaanta, sirf crypto envelope. src/types.ts: public types -- EntryInput, EntrySummary, EntryDetail, VaultExport, SharedEntryToken, DecryptedEntryBody. src/http/app.ts: createApp -- Express app, API-key middleware, saare routes, STATUS_BY_CODE mapping, asyncRoute wrapper, 404 fallback, error handler. src/http/server.ts: startServer -- listen aur graceful close. src/main.ts: npm start entry point, env vars se config. src/demo.ts: npm run demo, saare saat stages ek saath dikhata hai. test/: 17 test files -- crypto, vault, entries, change-password, export, generator, invariants (randomized), concurrency (actual races), breach, circuit-breaker, breach-checker, breach-integration, sharing, sharing-integration, share-revocation, session-idle-timeout, http.
difficult_decisions: Canary ciphertext master password verify karne ke liye, ek separate stored hash ke bajaye. Password hash store karna matlab do secrets (encryption key derivation aur verification hash) ko sync mein rakhna, jo drift kar sakte hain. Canary ek hi KDF reuse karta hai -- decrypt succeed ho jaaye matlab password sahi hai, AES-GCM ka authentication tag khud hi yeh guarantee deta hai, koi alag comparison zaroori nahi.

Race ko claim-before-await se prevent karna, lock primitive se nahi. JavaScript synchronous code ko kabhi preempt nahi karta, isliye agar claim (rotating check, pendingEntryOps++) synchronous hai aur koi await se pehle hota hai, to woh exclusion guaranteed hai by construction -- koi mutex library, koi retry logic nahi chahiye. Yeh pattern stage 2 mein entries ke liye bana, aur stage 5 mein shares ke liye bilkul wahi shape reuse hui, ek bilkul alag resource ke liye.

RSA-OAEP hybrid encryption, raw asymmetric encryption ke bajaye. RSA chhoti payload hi encrypt kar sakta hai aur slow hai, isliye sirf ek one-time AES key ko wrap karta hai; entry ka actual content AES-256-GCM se, poore project mein jahan bhi encryption hoti hai wahi scheme. Yeh TLS aur PGP jo karte hain, wahi pattern hai.

Idle session expiry lazy honi chahiye, background timer nahi. Lockout cooldown aur SESSION_INVALIDATED dono already lazy checks hain -- requireSession ke andar, next use par. Idle timeout ko bhi wahi jagah daalna matlab ek hi choke point se do kaam ho jaate hain, aur ek naya background job add nahi karna padta jiski apni correctness proof chahiye hogi.

Breach check kabhi save ko block nahi kar sakta -- yeh is project ke 'error means nothing happened' rule ka exception hai, jaan-boojh ke. BreachChecker.check() khud kabhi throw nahi karta; provider error, timeout, ya open circuit, sab null mein degrade ho jaate hain. Ek non-critical dependency kisi ko apna password save karne se rok nahi sakta.

Share grant ek manager-wide map mein, VaultRecord ke andar nahi. Yeh ek grant ke baare mein metadata hai, kisi ek vault ka content nahi -- wahi reasoning jo sessions ko already manager level par rakhti hai, vault ke andar nahi.
biggest_challenges: Stage 3 mein breach-check ka await claimEntryOp se PEHLE add karne se concurrency tests ka timing assumption toot gaya. addEntry pehle synchronously claim leta tha, turant; breach-check add karne ke baad, agar woh claim se pehle await ho jaaye to doosra concurrent call us claim ko dekh hi nahi pata time par. Fix: breach-check promise start karo claim se pehle (clock shuru ho jaaye), lekin await claim ke BAAD karo -- taaki claimEntryOp still synchronous aur sabse pehle rahe. Isi wajah se ek updateEntry-vs-deleteEntry concurrency test ka store.pending order bhi reverse ho gaya tha kyunki updateEntry ab breach-check ke through ek extra hop leta hai, deleteEntry nahi -- test ke comments aur indices fix karne pade.

Mutation testing ka ek 'survivor' asal mein mutation script ki apni galti thi, bug nahi. RV7 mutation ne NO_SHARING_KEY check ko claim ke baad move kiya, lekin wahan ek PEHLE wala, alag check already us code ko unreachable bana chuka tha -- koi test kabhi fark nahi dekh sakta tha kyunki record.wrappedPrivateKey do checks ke beech kuch badal hi nahi sakta. Discard kar diya, test nahi likha -- exact wahi principle jo stage 1 ke dead-code guard ke liye use hua tha.

HTTP lockout test mein 'wrong' password string use kiya, jo MIN_MASTER_PASSWORD_LENGTH (8) se chhota tha -- library ne usse length validation par hi 400 de diya, lockout counter tak pahunchi hi nahi. Expected 401 mila 400, jo pehli nazar mein library ka bug lagta tha. Fix sirf test mein, longer wrong password use karna -- sabak: test fixture ko system ke SAARE invariants satisfy karna chahiye, sirf jo test kar rahe ho usse nahi.

Buffer.prototype.map() TypeScript mein Uint8Array return karta hai, Buffer nahi -- isliye .toString('base64') call karne par type error aata (Uint8Array.toString() argument nahi leta). Yeh crypto.test.ts aur sharing.test.ts dono mein aaya jab tampered ciphertext/authTag/IV test karna tha. Fix: ek flipFirstByte helper jo Buffer.from() se wapas wrap karta hai.

Stage 4 ka ek real gap jo shipping se pehle pakda gaya: changeMasterPassword entries ko re-encrypt karta tha lekin wrappedPrivateKey ko re-wrap karna shuru mein design mein nahi socha gaya tha -- agar yeh ship hota, pehli password change ke baad sharing permanently toot jaata, private key purani key se encrypted reh jaata jabki canary nayi key maang rahi hoti. PLAN.md likhte waqt yeh explicitly call out kiya gaya aur code mein fix kiya gaya pehle commit se pehle.
failure_scenarios: VaultStore commit hang ho jaaye: withTimeout commitTimeoutMs (default 5000ms) ke baad AbortSignal fire karta hai, STORE_TIMEOUT throw hota hai, aur claim (pendingEntryOps ya rotating) finally block mein release ho jaata hai -- ek stuck commit poore vault ko permanently wedge nahi karta.

Breach-check provider down ya slow: CircuitBreaker 3 consecutive failures ke baad open ho jaata hai, aage ke calls provider ko bina call kiye hi fail-fast hote hain; check() hamesha null degrade karta hai, kabhi throw nahi -- save kabhi block nahi hota.
Share dobara redeem karne ki koshish: pehla claim synchronous hota hai, isliye doosra attempt turant SHARE_ALREADY_REDEEMED dekh leta hai, chahe woh bilkul saath mein (concurrent) ho ya baad mein.

Galat recipient apna private key use kare kisi doosre ke liye bheje gaye token par: RSA-OAEP unwrap fail hota hai, DECRYPTION_FAILED milta hai, aur claim release ho jaata hai -- asli recipient abhi bhi successfully redeem kar sakta hai baad mein.
Session idle ho jaaye: next use par SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT, session lazily cleanup ho jaata hai. isSessionActive() yeh bina side-effect ke batata hai, polling se session zinda nahi rehta.
5 galat master password attempts: LOCKED_OUT, LOCKOUT_MS (30s) tak koi aur attempt accept nahi hota, chahe sahi password ho. changeMasterPassword bhi isi gate se guzarta hai.
improvements: Real persistence: VaultStore abhi in-memory hai; real disk/database backend abhi tak nahi likha gaya, sirf interface design hai.
Sharing public keys ke liye directory service: abhi callers ko out-of-band public key exchange karna padta hai, project yeh handoff model nahi karta.
2FA, aur password-strength scoring beyond generator ke apne charset rules -- abhi nahi hai.
HTTP API par CORS, per-end-user session/cookie layer, aur rate limiting apne aap nahi hai -- yeh sirf ek service-level API key authenticate karta hai, browser-facing nahi hai.
Idle session cleanup proactive nahi, lazy hai -- memory mein idle sessions tab tak baithi rehti hain jab tak koi unhe touch na kare.
Share revocation sirf redeem se PEHLE kaam karta hai -- ek baar redeem ho jaaye, recipient ki copy permanent aur independent hai, usse wapas revoke nahi kiya ja sakta.

steps: 1. Concept: master password kabhi store nahi hota, na hashed. Ek fixed plaintext (canary) vault banate waqt derived key se encrypt hoti hai; unlock par candidate key se decrypt try hota hai -- AES-GCM ka authentication tag khud pass/fail signal hai.
2. Project need: agar password hash alag se store karte, to encryption key derivation aur verification hash dono sync mein rakhne padte, jo drift kar sakte hain. Ek hi KDF output dono kaam karta hai.
3. Code/API: crypto.ts deriveKey (scrypt), encrypt/decrypt (AES-256-GCM); manager.ts verifyMasterPassword, createVault, unlock.

4. Detail: CANARY_PLAINTEXT ek fixed buffer hai; wrong key se decrypt fail hota hai kyunki auth tag match nahi karta, Node khud exception throw karta hai; failedAttempts aur lockedUntil isi function mein track hote hain.

5. Demo: cd projects/23-password-manager && npx vitest run test/vault.test.ts test/crypto.test.ts -- 'the wrong master password throws INVALID_MASTER_PASSWORD', 'decrypting with the wrong key throws DECRYPTION_FAILED instead of returning garbage'.
6. Interviewer next: agar scrypt cost parameters bahut high set kar doon to kya hoga, aur canary approach mein salt reuse ka risk kya hai?

learning_path.concept: Encrypted entry storage, lockout, and the 'an error means nothing happened' rule
steps: 1. Concept: har credential entry ek AES-256-GCM blob hai, fresh IV ke saath har baar; lockout 5 wrong attempts ke baad; validation hamesha state change se PEHLE, taaki ek galat request kuch bhi badle bina fail ho.
2. Project need: agar IV reuse hota, to AES-GCM badly break ho jaata; agar validation state change ke baad hoti, to ek partial write ho sakti thi jab request galat thi.
3. Code/API: manager.ts addEntry, updateEntry, deleteEntry, requireString, requireEntry; crypto.ts encrypt (naya IV har call).

4. Detail: changeMasterPassword's own password check unlock() ke SAME lockout gate se guzarta hai, taaki woh guessing ka unrated side door na bane; updateEntry sirf diye gaye fields patch karta hai, baaki existing body se merge hote hain.

5. Demo: cd projects/23-password-manager && npx vitest run test/entries.test.ts test/change-password.test.ts -- 'an invalid patch throws and leaves the entry completely unchanged', 'a wrong old password counts against the SAME lockout as unlock()'.
6. Interviewer next: agar lockout per-IP ki jagah per-account ho to distributed denial-of-service kaise roka jaaye?

learning_path.concept: Multiple devices, one vault: sessions and the claim-before-await concurrency pattern
steps: 1. Concept: unlock() ek sessionId deta hai, vault ko locked/unlocked nahi maanta jaata. Har mutation apne ek await ko ek SYNCHRONOUS claim se wrap karta hai -- JavaScript synchronous code preempt nahi karta, isliye yeh exclusion by construction guaranteed hai, lock primitive se nahi.
2. Project need: phone aur laptop dono same vault par kaam kar sakte hain; ek device lock kare to doosra affected nahi hona chahiye; aur do concurrent writes ek doosre ko corrupt nahi karni chahiye.
3. Code/API: manager.ts claimEntryOp, commit, requireSession; VaultRecord ke rotating aur pendingEntryOps fields.

4. Detail: claimEntryOp koi await se pehle chalta hai -- rotating check karta hai, pendingEntryOps++ karta hai; commit succeed hone ke baad hi in-memory state (record.entries) update hoti hai, finally block mein claim release hota hai chahe success ho ya fail.

5. Demo: cd projects/23-password-manager && npx vitest run test/vault.test.ts -t 'sessions' test/concurrency.test.ts -t 'adding' -- 'two devices can unlock the SAME vault at once', 'two devices adding entries at the same time'.
6. Interviewer next: yeh pattern ek distributed system (multiple server instances) mein kaam karega kya, ya sirf single-process guarantee hai?

learning_path.concept: The lost-update bug a rotation's wholesale replace can cause, and the fix
steps: 1. Concept: changeMasterPassword har entry ko purani key se decrypt, nayi key se re-encrypt karta hai, ek NAYE Map mein -- aur record.entries ko tabhi replace karta hai jab commit succeed ho jaaye.

2. Project need: agar koi addEntry rotation ke BEECH mein land kare, bina claim ke, uska naya entry (purani key se encrypted) rotation ke wholesale replace se silently discard ho jaata -- yeh exact bug jo pendingEntryOps/rotating prevent karte hain.
3. Code/API: manager.ts changeMasterPassword, claimEntryOp; test/concurrency.test.ts ka 'the bug this design prevents' illustration (PasswordManager use nahi karta, sirf concept dikhata hai).
4. Detail: rotating true hone par koi naya addEntry claim turant VAULT_BUSY deta hai; pendingEntryOps zero na ho to rotation khud turant VAULT_BUSY deta hai -- dono directions guarded.

5. Demo: cd projects/23-password-manager && npx vitest run test/concurrency.test.ts -t 'rotation' -- 'addEntry started WHILE a rotation is in flight', 'changeMasterPassword started WHILE an addEntry is in flight'.
6. Interviewer next: agar yeh exclusion na hoti, is bug ko production mein kaise detect karte (koi log, koi metric)?

learning_path.concept: k-anonymity breach checking and a circuit breaker that can never block a save
steps: 1. Concept: breach-check sirf password ke SHA-1 hash ka 5-char prefix bahar bhejta hai; provider wahi prefix share karne wale saare breached hashes ka suffix list deta hai, comparison locally hoti hai. Yeh exact wahi protocol hai jo Have I Been Pwned's real API use karta hai.
2. Project need: breach-check ek non-critical dependency hai -- agar yeh down ho, user ko password save karne se rok nahi sakta. Isliye check() kabhi throw nahi karta, hamesha null degrade karta hai.
3. Code/API: breach.ts sha1Hex, isPasswordBreached, FakeBreachProvider; circuit-breaker.ts CircuitBreaker; breach-checker.ts BreachChecker.check.

4. Detail: CircuitBreaker closed se open (3 consecutive failures), open se half-open (cooldown ke baad ek trial), success par wapas closed; breachCheck promise addEntry mein claimEntryOp se PEHLE start hoti hai (clock shuru ho jaaye) lekin AWAIT claim ke BAAD hota hai, taaki claim abhi bhi sabse pehla synchronous kaam rahe.

5. Demo: cd projects/23-password-manager && npx vitest run test/breach.test.ts test/circuit-breaker.test.ts test/breach-checker.test.ts test/breach-integration.test.ts -- 'never sends more than a 5-character prefix', 'a broken breach-check provider never blocks addEntry or updateEntry'.
6. Interviewer next: agar breach-check service rate-limit kare, circuit breaker ke threshold values kaise tune karoge?

learning_path.concept: Hybrid/envelope encryption: sharing one entry between two independent vaults
steps: 1. Concept: RSA-OAEP sirf chhoti payload encrypt kar sakta hai aur slow hai, isliye sirf ek fresh one-time AES key wrap karta hai; entry ka actual content AES-256-GCM se, poore project jaisa. TLS aur PGP yahi pattern use karte hain.

2. Project need: ek credential doosre vault ko securely bhejna hai, bina kisi vault ke master password ya symmetric key doosre ko bataye. Har vault apni RSA keypair lazily banata hai -- 2048-bit keygen ~200ms leta hai, isliye har createVault par nahi, sirf first getSharingPublicKey call par.
3. Code/API: sharing.ts generateSharingKeyPair, sealForRecipient, openAsRecipient; manager.ts getSharingPublicKey, shareEntry, redeemShare.

4. Detail: shareEntry pure synchronous hai (koi commit nahi, sender ka vault badalta nahi); redeemShare unwrap karke seedha recipient ka apna addEntry call karta hai -- isliye recipient ki apni breach-check config aur apna claim/commit use hota hai, koi duplicate logic nahi.

5. Demo: cd projects/23-password-manager && npx vitest run test/sharing.test.ts test/sharing-integration.test.ts -- 'bob ends up with his own copy of alice's entry', 'the share token never contains the plaintext password, title or username in the clear'.
6. Interviewer next: agar RSA ki jagah elliptic curve (ECIES) use karte, kya extra complexity aati?

1. Concept: har shareEntry call ek grant register karta hai ek manager-wide shares map mein (shareId -> ownerId, revoked, redeemedAt). redeemShare is grant ko synchronously claim karta hai -- bilkul claimEntryOp jaisa pattern, ek alag resource ke liye.
2. Project need: ek share token sirf ek baar redeem hona chahiye -- same token dobara redeem karna duplicate entries banata. Aur sender ko apna mind badalne ka mauka chahiye, redeem hone se pehle.
3. Code/API: manager.ts revokeShare, redeemShare -- share.redeemedAt = this.clock.now() (claim) aur catch block mein release.

4. Detail: NO_SHARING_KEY check claim se PEHLE hota hai (setup na hone ki galti ek legitimate chance nahi khaani chahiye); DECRYPTION_FAILED ya recipient ka apna VAULT_BUSY claim ke BAAD aata hai, toh release hota hai -- real retry bacha rehta hai; revokeShare unknown aur someone-else's shareId identically UNKNOWN_SHARE deta hai.

5. Demo: cd projects/23-password-manager && npx vitest run test/share-revocation.test.ts -- 'two concurrent redemptions of the SAME token: exactly one succeeds', 'someone else's shareId also throws UNKNOWN_SHARE'.
6. Interviewer next: agar ek share link ko expiry time (jaise 24 hours) bhi dena ho, kahan add karoge?

learning_path.concept: Session auto-lock via lazy idle expiry
steps: 1. Concept: session sessionIdleTimeoutMs ke baad idle maana jaata hai, LAZILY -- next use par check hota hai, background timer kabhi nahi. requireSession yeh check karta hai aur same jagah successful use par lastActivityAt reset karta hai.

2. Project need: ek credential manager mein bohot der tak unlocked session khula rehna ek real security gap hai. Lekin ek background sweep add karna extra complexity hai jiski apni correctness proof chahiye.
3. Code/API: manager.ts requireSession, isSessionActive; Session interface ka lastActivityAt field.

4. Detail: isSessionActive EK PURE READ hai, kabhi lastActivityAt reset nahi karta -- warna sirf status poll karte rehna session ko zinda rakh deta, jo feature ka poora point khatam kar deta; har session ka apna independent idle clock hai, ek device idle ho to doosra affected nahi hota.

5. Demo: cd projects/23-password-manager && npx vitest run test/session-idle-timeout.test.ts -- 'polling isSessionActive does NOT itself reset the clock', 'two sessions on one vault have independent idle clocks'.
6. Interviewer next: agar activity ko explicitly track karna ho (jaise sirf writes count karni hain, reads nahi), design kaise badlega?

learning_path.concept: HTTP API: one API key, and mapping every library error to a status code
steps: 1. Concept: service-to-service API ek shared secret (Bearer key) se authenticate, constant-time compare se. Har PasswordManagerErrorCode ek specific HTTP status par map hota hai -- koi bhi library error 500 nahi, kyunki sab expected outcomes hain.

2. Project need: caller ko pata hona chahiye ki galti kiski hai (400 uska, 503 hamara dependency); aur Express 4 khud rejected promise ko error handler tak nahi le jaata, isliye async routes ko explicitly wrap karna padta hai.
3. Code/API: http/app.ts createApp, STATUS_BY_CODE, asyncRoute, keyMatches; http/server.ts startServer.

4. Detail: auth middleware body parse hone se PEHLE chalta hai; POST .../shares/redeem ka body structurally check hota hai HTTP layer mein hi, kyunki library ka koi equivalent check nahi hai us specific case ke liye -- warna malformed body openAsRecipient tak ek raw TypeError ke roop mein pahunchta.

5. Demo: cd projects/23-password-manager && npx vitest run test/http.test.ts -- 'rejects a request with no API key', 'an unexpected (non-library) error maps to 500 and is logged, not leaked to the caller'.
6. Interviewer next: per-caller API keys aur scopes kaise add karoge, aur multi-tenant SaaS ke liye yeh model kaise evolve hoga?

learning_path.concept: Testing honestly: randomized invariants and mutation checks
steps: 1. Concept: randomized invariant test = random operations chalao ek shadow model ke against, har step par independently re-derive karke check karo. Mutation check = jaan-boojh ke ek line todo, suite chalao, dekho koi test fail hota hai ya nahi, file byte-for-byte restore karo.
2. Project need: concurrency x sharing x revocation x idle-timeout ke combinations haath ke tests cover nahi karte, aur '140 tests pass' yeh nahi batata ki tests kuch pakadte hain.
3. Code/API: test/invariants.test.ts (4 seeds x 150 sequential operations), test/concurrency.test.ts (actual races, FakeVaultStore se controlled interleaving), README.md ki mutation tables.

4. Detail: 128 mutation checks, sab caught, ek chhod ke jo khud malformed thi (discard kiya, test nahi likha); genuine survivors mile the -- ek double-delete race, ek rotation jo persisted snapshot mein purana salt/canary bhej sakti thi while in-memory sahi tha, ek leaked timer, circuit breaker ka success failure-counter reset na karna, aur default idle timeout kabhi exercise na hona -- sab fix kiye gaye naye tests se, chhupaye nahi gaye.
5. Demo: cd projects/23-password-manager && npm test (140 tests), aur npx vitest run test/invariants.test.ts test/concurrency.test.ts.
6. Interviewer next: ek mutation jo 'malformed' lage (genuinely unreachable) aur ek jo 'test gap' ho, dono ke beech kaise pehchanoge?
